alalal-e81289-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 12: whether faith is one or differs according to the things believed, as science differs by its objects.

alalal-e81289-d1e117.summary: Introduces the question on Lombard's chapter 'Cumque diversis modis dicatur fides'.

alalal-e81289-d1e129.summary: First objection: faith involves knowledge, which differs by its objects, so faith differs by the credibles, which are many, the twelve or fourteen articles of the creeds.

alalal-e81289-d1e154.summary: Second objection: wisdom and knowledge differ as being about the eternal and the temporal; faith concerns both, so it is diverse.

alalal-e81289-d1e172.summary: Third objection: fear of eternal punishment differs from love and hope of eternal good, so faith about punishments differs from faith about glory.

alalal-e81289-d1e194.summary: Fourth objection: saying faith lies in the will's affection rather than cognition does not help, since wills also differ by their objects.

alalal-e81289-d1e212.summary: Sed contra: in all the articles first truth is presupposed as the essential and final object of belief, and it is one, so faith is one.

alalal-e81289-d1e225.summary: Further question on Lombard's saying that the faith by which one believes is one in genus, not in species: it seems one in species, differing in different believers only materially.

alalal-e81289-d1e244.summary: Solution: faith is numerically one in its ratio and first object, since the ratio of believing in all articles is first truth, abstracted from each; I believe Christ suffered not because he suffered but because of first truth. But its subject as contracted and specified by the matter of the articles is not one; in that sense there are twelve or fourteen.
claims: Faith is one because its formal ratio and first object, first truth, is one in all articles.
Faith is materially many according to the content of the articles.
concepts: formal and material object of faith

alalal-e81289-d1e284.summary: Reply to the second: science takes its ratio from considering the temporal and wisdom from eternal reasons, so they differ; but faith believes the temporal not as temporal but as matter of the eternal and of first truth, so it takes no specific difference from it.

alalal-e81289-d1e308.summary: Reply to the third: fear is a simple fleeing affection taking its ratio from punishment as evil, opposed to hope of eternal good; faith concerns punishments not as evil but as subject to first truth, so articles of eternal punishment and of eternal glory do not differ for faith.

alalal-e81289-d1e341.summary: Reply to the fourth: even if faith is called an affection, it is not diversified, since it tends to diverse things by reason of the one thing underlying all, first truth.

alalal-e81289-d1e357.summary: Reply to the further question: Lombard calls 'genus' what is predicated of many species, the material species being taken from the multitude of articles. Some read 'one in genus' as one by generation. Or it is one in genus by reason of states, since the state of history diversifies articles as statements, though they are one in reality, as 'Christ is incarnate' and 'Christ will be incarnate'.

alalal-e81289.summary: Article 12 asks whether faith is one or differs according to its objects, as science does. Objections appeal to the many articles, to the distinction between eternal and temporal objects, to fear and hope differing by their objects, and to wills differing by what they will. Albert answers that faith is one in its formal ratio and first object, first truth, which underlies every article: one believes Christ suffered not because he suffered but because of first truth. Faith is many only materially, according to the content of the twelve or fourteen articles. Temporal articles and articles about punishment are believed as subject to first truth, not as temporal or evil, so they do not divide faith. Lombard's 'one in genus' refers to the material plurality of articles, or to the different historical states in which the same reality is stated differently.
claims: Faith is one because its formal object, first truth, is one in every article.
Faith is materially many according to the articles' content.
Temporal and penal articles are believed under first truth and do not divide faith.
